source_evidence: The issuer may fail to timely make interest or principal payments and thus default on its bonds.
answer: Credit risk is the possibility that a bond’s issuer will not make interest or principal payments on time. If the issuer defaults, promised payments may not arrive as scheduled. The source also notes that investment-grade corporate bonds have higher credit ratings and imply less credit risk than high-yield corporate bonds; high-yield bonds imply higher credit risk.
